body: Audiocraft is a library for audio processing and generation with deep learning. It features the state-of-the-art EnCodec audio compressor / tokenizer, along with MusicGen, a simple and controllable music generation LM with textual and melodic conditioning.
plain_description: Generate professional-quality music and audio from simple text descriptions using AudioCraft's AI models. MusicGen creates original compositions for content, advertising, and games; AudioGen produces custom sound effects on demand — without hiring composers or sound engineers. The bottom line: turn text prompts into studio-quality audio in seconds.
technical_description: AudioCraft is a PyTorch library for deep learning research and inference in audio generation. It provides training and inference implementations for MusicGen (text-to-music), AudioGen (text-to-sound), EnCodec (neural audio codec), Multi Band Diffusion, MAGNeT, AudioSeal, MusicGen Style, and JASCO. The library is installable via pip with Python 3.9+ and PyTorch 2.1.0, and requires ffmpeg for audio processing. Pretrained model weights are hosted on Hugging Face and downloaded on first use. AudioCraft supports training custom models through its configurable solver and grid-based pipeline system.
title: AudioCraft

plain_description: Bark turns written text into natural-sounding speech, music, and sound effects using AI. It supports multiple languages and can convey emotions like laughter or sighs to make audio sound authentic. The big picture: generate professional voiceovers and audio content from plain text, eliminating the need for recording studios or voice talent.
technical_description: Bark is a GPT-style transformer model for text-to-audio generation developed by Suno. It converts text prompts directly to audio waveforms using a quantized audio representation from EnCodec, bypassing traditional phoneme-based pipelines. The architecture follows AudioLM and Vall-E approaches, enabling generative capabilities beyond conventional TTS including music, sound effects, and nonverbal cues. Bark supports 100+ speaker presets across 13 languages, runs on CPU or NVIDIA GPU via PyTorch 2.0+, and offers both a direct Python API and Hugging Face Transformers integration (v4.31.0+). The full model requires ~12GB VRAM; a smaller variant (~8GB VRAM) is selectable via the SUNO_USE_SMALL_MODELS environment variable, with CPU offloading available for low-VRAM configurations.
title: Bark

body: A generative speech model for daily dialogue.
plain_description: ChatTTS brings natural, expressive voice to conversational AI applications like chatbots and virtual assistants. It's purpose-built for dialogue, letting you control tone, laughter, and pauses in generated speech. The bottom line: add lifelike voice output to your AI products without building a TTS system from scratch.
technical_description: ChatTTS is an open-source text-to-speech model optimized for dialogue-based synthesis. It uses an autoregressive architecture with a DVAE encoder and supports fine-grained prosodic control including laughter, pauses, and interjections via special tokens. The model is trained on over 100,000 hours of Chinese and English audio, with a 40,000-hour pre-trained checkpoint available on HuggingFace. It provides a Python API via PyPI, supports GPU acceleration on NVIDIA hardware, and includes a WebUI for interactive use.
title: ChatTTS

body: 🐸💬 - a deep learning toolkit for Text-to-Speech, battle-tested in research and production
plain_description: The big picture: generate natural-sounding speech from text with a production-ready toolkit that supports over 1,100 languages. Here's why it matters: you can fine-tune existing models or train custom voices for your specific use case without building a TTS engine from scratch. The bottom line: add realistic voice synthesis to your product quickly and reliably.
technical_description: 🐸TTS is an open-source deep learning library for Text-to-Speech synthesis. It implements multiple model architectures including Tacotron2, Glow-TTS, VITS, and XTTS for spectrogram generation and end-to-end synthesis, paired with vocoders such as HiFiGAN, WaveGrad, and WaveRNN for waveform generation. The library provides a Python API and CLI for inference, multi-speaker voice cloning, voice conversion, and model fine-tuning. Models are implemented in PyTorch and support inference on CPU and NVIDIA GPU. Deployment is available via pip install or Docker images that include an HTTP server for remote inference.
title: TTS

plain_description: Fish Speech delivers studio-quality voice generation in 80+ languages — the most powerful open-source text-to-speech engine you can run yourself. Clone any voice from just 10 seconds of audio and control emotion, tone, and delivery with simple text commands. No phonemes, no complex setup, no ongoing API costs.
technical_description: Fish Speech (Fish Audio S2 Pro) is a state-of-the-art multilingual text-to-speech system built on a Dual-Autoregressive (Dual-AR) transformer architecture. The model comprises a slow AR with 4 billion parameters operating on the time axis to predict the primary semantic codebook, and a fast AR with 400 million parameters generating nine residual codebooks per time step using an RVQ audio codec with 10 codebooks at approximately 21 Hz. Trained on over 10 million hours of audio across 80-plus languages, S2 Pro supports sub-word level prosody control through natural language tags and natively handles multi-speaker and multi-turn generation. Inference acceleration via SGLang provides continuous batching, paged KV cache, and RadixAttention prefix caching, achieving a real-time factor of 0.195 and time-to-first-audio of approximately 100 milliseconds on a single NVIDIA H200 GPU. Deployment options include Docker, command-line interface, WebUI, and REST API server. Voice cloning is supported from reference samples of 10 to 30 seconds without requiring additional fine-tuning.
title: Fish Speech

plain_description: Kokoro delivers high-quality text-to-speech with a lightweight 82-million-parameter model that runs fast and costs little. It's Apache-licensed, so you can deploy it anywhere from production servers to personal projects without licensing headaches.
technical_description: Kokoro is an inference library for the Kokoro-82M open-weight TTS model. It provides a KPipeline class that handles grapheme-to-phoneme conversion via the misaki library and generates 24kHz audio output. The library supports multiple languages including American English, British English, Spanish, French, Hindi, Italian, Japanese, Brazilian Portuguese, and Mandarin Chinese. It integrates with PyTorch for model execution and can be installed via pip.
title: kokoro

body: Moshi is a speech-text foundation model and full-duplex spoken dialogue framework. It uses Mimi, a state-of-the-art streaming neural audio codec.
plain_description: Moshi enables real-time voice conversations with AI by processing speech and text simultaneously. It understands what you say and responds in under 200 milliseconds while you are still talking, making interactions feel natural. Run it on your own infrastructure with Docker or deploy on Apple devices with MLX acceleration.
technical_description: Moshi is a 7B-parameter speech-text foundation model implementing full-duplex spoken dialogue. It uses the Mimi streaming neural audio codec (12.5 Hz frame rate, 1.1 kbps bandwidth, 80 ms latency) to process 24 kHz audio. The architecture combines a Depth Transformer for inter-codebook dependencies with a Temporal Transformer for temporal modeling. Three implementations are available: PyTorch (research, requires 24 GB GPU), MLX (Apple Silicon on-device inference), and Rust/Candle (production, CUDA or Metal acceleration). Deployment options include Docker Compose, pip-installable packages, and a web UI with echo cancellation.
title: Moshi

body: Instant voice cloning by MIT and MyShell. Audio foundation model.
plain_description: Clone any voice instantly with OpenVoice — generate natural-sounding speech in multiple languages from just a short audio sample. Backed by MIT research and used millions of times on MyShell's platform, it delivers accurate tone reproduction with fine-grained control over emotion and speaking style. The bottom line: high-quality voice cloning that's free for commercial use.
technical_description: OpenVoice is an audio foundation model for instant voice cloning developed by MIT and MyShell. It performs zero-shot cross-lingual voice cloning from a reference audio sample and supports granular control over voice styles including emotion, accent, rhythm, pauses, and intonation. Version 2 (V2) improves audio quality and natively supports English, Spanish, French, Chinese, Japanese, and Korean. The implementation builds on TTS, VITS, and VITS2 frameworks. Both V1 and V2 are released under the MIT License.
title: OpenVoice

body: Inference and training library for high-quality TTS models.
plain_description: Parler-TTS generates high-quality, natural-sounding speech from text using simple descriptions to control voice characteristics like gender, pitch, and speaking style. Fully open-source with pre-trained models ready to use — no expensive API subscriptions required. Fine-tune on your own speakers for customized voice output.
technical_description: Parler-TTS is a text-to-speech model implemented in PyTorch using the Hugging Face Transformers library. It uses a conditional generation architecture that encodes both a text prompt and a natural language description of speaker characteristics to produce speech audio. The repository provides inference and training pipelines with support for SDPA, Flash Attention 2, torch.compile, and streaming generation. Pre-trained checkpoints at 880M (Mini) and 2.3B (Large) parameters are available, trained on 45k hours of audiobook data. The training pipeline supports fine-tuning on single-speaker datasets using Hugging Face Accelerate.
title: Parler-TTS

body: A fast, local neural text to speech system
plain_description: Piper turns text into speech locally on your own machine — no cloud, no data leaving your system. It runs fast on consumer hardware and costs nothing per use. The bottom line: private, offline neural TTS with no ongoing fees.
technical_description: Piper is a neural text-to-speech inference engine written in C++ that runs entirely on local hardware without cloud dependencies. It is optimized for CPU execution and a Docker image is available for deployment. Development of this repository has moved to the OHF-Voice organization.
title: Piper

body: Easily train a good VC model with voice data <= 10 mins!
plain_description: Train a convincing voice conversion model with only 10 minutes of speech data and run it in real time on your own computer — no cloud fees or AI expertise required. The web interface lets you transform any source voice into any target voice with sub-200ms latency. This open-source tool is MIT-licensed, free to use commercially, and runs on everything from gaming GPUs to integrated laptop chips.
technical_description: RVC is a Python-based framework for retrieval-based voice conversion that uses a top-1 feature retrieval mechanism to replace source speaker embeddings with training-set features, eliminating timbre leakage. The pipeline combines a HuBERT content encoder for semantic feature extraction, RMVPE for F0 pitch extraction, and a HiFi-GAN vocoder for waveform synthesis. It provides a Gradio-based WebUI with separate interfaces for model training and real-time voice changing, supporting end-to-end latencies as low as 90ms with ASIO audio drivers. Training requires as little as 10 minutes of clean speech data and runs on NVIDIA GPUs (CUDA 11.8/12.8), AMD and Intel GPUs via DirectML on Windows, or CPU-only mode.
title: Retrieval-based-Voice-Conversion-WebUI

plain_description: Transform any singing voice into another voice while preserving natural pitch, intonation, and expression — no original singer needed. This open-source tool lets creators generate custom vocal performances entirely offline on their own hardware, keeping all data private. The bottom line: anyone with a computer and a voice dataset can create a personalized singing voice model.
technical_description: so-vits-svc is an open-source singing voice conversion (SVC) framework built on a modified VITS architecture. It uses a SoftVC content encoder to extract speech features from source audio, feeding them directly into the VITS decoder without intermediate text representation, preserving original pitch and intonation. The vocoder is replaced with NSF HiFiGAN to eliminate sound interruption artifacts. The framework supports multiple speech encoders (ContentVec, hubertsoft, Whisper-PPG, WavLM, DPHuBERT, CNHubert), F0 predictors (crepe, dio, pm, harvest, rmvpe, fcpe), and optional shallow diffusion post-processing. Inference is performed via Python CLI with support for pitch shifting, speaker mixing, feature retrieval, and ONNX export. The project operates fully offline with no telemetry.
title: SoftVC VITS Singing Voice Conversion
